narrative: Background:_x000D_ The Deep Orient is conducting Subsea Installation operations on the Prelude OIC2. On 08/10/2016 ROV XLX74 experienced an incident where the Forward Port Lateral Thruster Hydraulic Hose B2 ruptured during subsea operations causing loss of power to the thrusters and 3ltes of hydraulic oil to be lost to the sea (Synergi report 511732 refers). Another hose failure of the same hydraulic hose occurred on XLX 75 on 10/10/2016 (Synergi no.511956 refers). In both incidents the cause has been suspected as due to poor routing of the hydraulic hose on the vehicle which is causing the hose to rupture internally._x000D_ _x000D_ Environmental Conditions:_x000D_ Vessel maintaining position with good visibility at night, calm sea with significant wave height of 0.5m. Wind speed 4KN. Subsea visibility conditions were workable with a current of 1.7KN on the surface DP desk monitor. _x000D_ _x000D_ Task / Actions Leading up to the Incident:_x000D_ ROV XLX75 had completed disconnection of brace rigging on MJ1. The ROV was then in preparation to commence connecting tagging rigging to brace._x000D_ _x000D_ Incident/Initial findings:_x000D_ At 19:10 at depth of 50m during operations to initiate Tag lines to Spreader bar for recovery to surface, the current at the working depth had increased which was hampering ROV XLX 75 ability to maintain required position/station to conduct works. _x000D_ Whilst trying to maintain station at the worksite and keep the ROV in a safe position the ROV had to be operated at 100% joystick control and full system pressure. _x000D_ During these manoeuvres the Port Aft (Lower) Lateral Thruster Hose ruptured and failed._x000D_ At time of hose failure the works had been suspended due to an unexpected excessive current, spreader was then lowered to 100m to check conditions, current improving.._x000D_ ROV XLX75 team made preparations to return defective sub to TMS, conditions at 50m not suitable to recover ROV to TMS, lowered TMS to 170m effecting safe recovery of ROV; ROV XLX on deck 19:44_x000D_ _x000D_ It is estimated that approx. 3 litres of T32 hydraulic oil was discharged from the vehicle into the sea during the event._x000D_ _x000D_ The immediate cause of the loss of hydraulic oil has been determined as a Port Aft (Lower) Lateral Thruster Hose failure._x000D_ _x000D_ It has been identified that the hydraulic hose has failed in the same area as 2 previous incidents which has further confirmed a routing issue with the hoses._x000D_ _x000D_ The hydraulic hose used on both vehicles is a Parker 471 ST Hydraulic Hose with 2-wire braided compact construction See details below._x000D_ _x000D_ Evidence of planned maintenance and pre-dive checks have identified that there were no externally visual signs of wear, deformity or damage to the hose._x000D_ _x000D_ RIS Regional Manager TMOS/Subsea Operations APAC has been advised of all incidents.
case_categorization: Substances  - Hazardous liquids (exposure to / spill / loss of containment /pollution)
